problem: Consider the function $f(x)={x}^{3}+\sqrt{x}.$ For which of the following values of $k$ does the intermediate value theorem **not** guarantee that $f(x)=k$ has a solution on the interval $[1,4]?$

feedback.problem: Consider the function $f(x)=(x+1)^{2}-4.$ For which of the following values of $k$ does the intermediate value theorem guarantee that $f(x)=k$ has a solution on the interval $x\in [-4,-2]?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The function $f(x)$ is continuous on $[-4,-2],$ so the intermediate value theorem guarantees that $f(x)=k$ has a solution for each value of $k$ between $f(-4)$ and $f(-2).$

Since $f(-4)=5$ and $f(-2)=-3,$ we must have 
$k\in [-3,5].$

Among the given options, only $k=2$ belongs to the interval $[-3,5].$
